{{nihongo|'''Atsuto Suzuki'''|鈴木 厚人|Suzuki Atsuto| born October 3, 1946, in [[Niigata Prefecture]], Japan}} is an experimental particle physicist known for his observations of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos.

== Career ==
[[File:Atsuto Suzuki and Piermaria Oddone 200704.jpg|thumb|left|200px|With [[Piermaria Oddone]] (April, 2007)]]
Suzuki earned his doctorate from [[Tohoku University]] in 1974, supervised by [[Masatoshi Koshiba]]. In 1982 he was appointed to the faculty of the [[Tokyo University|Tōkyō University]]. In 1993, he took concurrent positions as professor at the High Energy Physics Laboratory of Tohoku University and professor at the Institute of Cosmic Ray Research (ICRR) of Tōkyō University. Having taken part in the [[Kamiokande-II]] and [[Super-Kamiokande]] neutrino detection experiments, Suzuki was appointed Director of the Research Center for Neutrino Science in 1998 and led the [[KamLAND]] neutrino detection experiments. From 2006 until 2015 he was Director General of the [[KEK|High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)]] Accelerator Laboratory.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.bureau.tohoku.ac.jp/koho/pub/annual_review/tu2006-english.pdf| title=Tohoku University Annual Review| year=2006| page=5|access-date=19 September 2018}}</ref> Suzuki chaired the International Committee for Future Accelerators, a working group of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]], from 2009 to 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Membership {{!}} ICFA |url=https://icfa.hep.net/membership/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Scientific achievements ==
[[File:Atsuto Suzuki and Piermaria Oddone 201010.jpg|thumb|left|200px|With [[Piermaria Oddone]] (October, 2010)]]
The Kamiokande-II experiment detected a burst of neutrinos from [[Supernova 1987A]], the first observation of this kind, winning the research team the [[Asahi Prize|Asahi]] and [[Bruno Rossi Prize|Bruno Rossi]] prizes.<ref name="Asahi"/><ref name="Rossi">{{cite web | title=HEAD AAS Rossi Prize Winners | website=High Energy Astrophysics Division | url=https://head.aas.org/rossi/rossi.recip.html | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

Observations from the Super-Kamiokande experiment measured the phenomenon of [[neutrino oscillation]] (and hence neutrino mass) with unprecedented accuracy, thereby resolving the [[solar neutrino problem]].<ref name="Solar neutrinos">{{cite web| title=Solar Neutrinos| website=Super-Kamiokande| url=http://www-sk.icrr.u-tokyo.ac.jp/sk/sk/solar-e.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> For this accomplishment, the project was awarded the 1998 [[Asahi Prize]].<ref name="Asahi">{{cite web| author=The Asahi Shimbun Company| title=The Asahi Prize - English Information| website=The Asahi Shimbun Company| url=http://www.asahi.com/shimbun/award/asahi/english.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

The KamLAND experiment was the first to detect [[geoneutrinos]] generated by the decay of radionuclides deep inside Earth.[[File:AtsutoSuzuki-Neutel90.jpg|thumb|277x277px|Atsuto Suzuki talking about solar neutrinos at the Neutrino Telescopes Workshop, Venice, 1990]] These observations provided the first direct measurements of the abundance of geoneutrino-producing elements and their spatial distribution in Earth's interior, marking the start of a new field of neutrino geoscience.<ref name="Physics World 2005">{{cite web | title=Geoneutrinos make their debut – Physics World | website=Physics World | date=27 July 2005 | url=https://physicsworld.com/a/geoneutrinos-make-their-debut/ | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

== Awards ==

Suzuki received the Japanese [[Medals of Honor (Japan)#Purple ribbon|Medal of Honor with purple ribbon]] in 2005,<ref name="Medal">{{cite web | title=Professor Atsuko Suzuki (Vice President, Tohoku University, Director of Neutrino Science Research Center attached to the Graduate School of Science) received the Purple Ribbon Emblem of Fall 2005 | website=RCNS in Tohoku Univ. | url=http://www.awa.tohoku.ac.jp/KamLAND/prize_j.html | language=ja | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> the [[Bruno Pontecorvo Prize]] in 2006,<ref name="KEK 2007">{{cite web | title=Bruno Pontecorvo Prize was awarded to Dr. Suzuki | website=KEK | date=19 January 2007 | url=http://www2.kek.jp/en/topics/2007/BrunoPontecorvo_e.html | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> and the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] in 2016, shared with investigators from the [[KamLAND]], [[Super-Kamiokande]], [[K2K]] / [[T2K]], [[Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment|Daya Bay]], and [[Sudbury Neutrino Observatory|Sudbury]] neutrino observation consortia.<ref name="Breakthrough Prize 2016">{{cite web | title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Atsuto Suzuki and the KamLAND Collaboration | website=Breakthrough Prize | date=1 October 2016 | url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L154 | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> He was elected a foreign member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name="RAS">{{cite web| title=Suzuki, Atsuto| website=Russian Academy of Sciences| url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-61982.ln-ru| language=ru| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

In 2021, he was elected as a [[Person of Cultural Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2021102600557&g=pol|title= 長嶋茂雄さんら9人文化勲章 功労者に加山雄三さんら|access-date= October 26, 2021|work= Jiji.com|archive-date= October 26, 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211026070024/https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2021102600557&g=pol|url-status= dead}}</ref>

In 2022, he was elected as a Members of the [[Japan Academy]].<ref name="acad">[https://www.japan-acad.go.jp/japanese/news/2022/121201.html?fbclid=IwAR24JFPe3Zq0cmwtaWiPo7LkOICJmsDLFVxY2u5ldzkRSLCb0ttZ0-WCDT0 日本学士院会員の選定について | 日本学士院]</ref>
